titulo: 20% off plus an extra 20% off is not 40% off
receta: cuenta simple con la plata de todos los días + regla para guardar (se multiplica lo que queda), con fecha: Black Friday 11/27
destinatario: Se lo manda alguien que hace bien las cuentas a su amigo que dice que todo está 'casi a mitad de precio' en Black Friday.

interaccion.guardar: Stacked discounts multiply what's left: 20% off + 20% off = 0.8 x 0.8 = 64% of the price, so 36% off. A $100 item costs $64, not $60.
interaccion.comentar: What's the biggest discount you ever scored? Give me a percent.

frases.texto: Twenty percent off, plus an extra twenty percent off? That is not forty percent off.

frases.estilo: Dry and punchy, with a half smile.

frases.texto: Take a hundred-dollar jacket. The first twenty percent off leaves it at eighty dollars.
The extra twenty comes off the eighty, not the hundred. That's sixteen dollars, so you pay sixty-four.
Heads up: that's for deals that stack one after another. Some stores take the extra off the original price, so check the fine print.
The trick to save: multiply what's left. Eighty percent times eighty percent is sixty-four percent.
So what's the biggest discount you ever scored? Give me a percent.
Send this to the friend who says everything is basically half off.
